at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Round monetary values only via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.title: Normalize money via to_money and round_money
at-0002.content: Always convert incoming monetary values with `to_money(...)` and round with `round_money(...)` from `ledgerly.money` before storing them on models; compare against `ZERO` for sign checks.

at-0003.title: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes
at-0003.content: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with snake_case codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`; pass `repr(value)` as the detail.

at-0004.title: Guard mutations with draft status check
at-0004.content: Mutating invoice operations must first check `invoice.status != "draft"` and raise `BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}")`, matching `issue_invoice`.

at-0005.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
at-0005.content: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py` does for `at` and `sub.started_at`).

at-0006.title: Compute periods via timedelta floor division
at-0006.content: Compute subscription period boundaries the same way `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py` does: `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` then `n = (at - start) // length`, rather than manual day math.
